critical_steps: The displayed S is a nonzero idempotent Drazin inverse of K with K^2=S.
The coefficient energy is exactly ||K^* f||^2, so A=1 is a valid lower bound.
The printed A/||S|| bound fails at f=(1,0,-1).
Idempotence and the Drazin identities imply S*=S*K*, yielding the valid A/||S||^2 bound.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact finite-dimensional Drazin identities, an exact one-component K-g-fusion system, and a closed-form lower-bound minimization.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made that A/||S||^2 is the optimal lower bound for every individual frame.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects the quantitative lower bound in Corollary 3.10 and does not dispute its qualitative frame-preservation conclusion.
Sharpness is asserted for the universal norm-only bound; individual frames may admit larger lower bounds.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same exponent repair.
title: An idempotent Drazin inverse needs a squared norm in the \(K\)-\(g\)-fusion lower bound
